newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo naphtha firmer, spreads slightly narrowed.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo naphtha firmer, spreads slightly narrowed.

text.p: Naphtha prices bounced back in afternoon Tokyo trade, supported by day-time crude gains, traders said on Thursday.
First-half January open-spec naphtha, the most actively traded, was assessed at $219.50/$221.00, up from Wednesday's $217.50/$218.50.
Second-half December was assessed $1.00 higher and first-half December indicated around $2.00 higher than the first-half January level, traders said.
Naphtha spreads were a touch narrower with second-half December/second-half January discussed at about plus $2.00.
With Aramco's term naphtha prices settled, naphtha importers have started negotiating with South Korean suppliers for 1997 cargoes, traders said.

In the low sulphur waxy residue (LSWR) market, levels for November cargoes were notionally assessed as low as 20 to 30 cents above the Pertamina formula, while wholesale prices of import cargoes remained higher than domestic lots.

Import cargo prices need to be $1.00 or $2.00 per barrel lower than the current levels to be competitive against low sulphur fuel oil cargoes produced at domestic refineries, traders said. -- Tokyo Energy Desk +81-3-3432-8837
